prompt: A two-column proof begins with the given equation $3x - 7 = 20$. Step 2 adds $7$ to both sides (Addition Property of Equality). Step 3 divides both sides by $3$ (Division Property of Equality). What value of $x$ does the proof reach?
hint: Follow the two steps exactly as the proof describes them.

hints.text: Follow the two steps exactly as the proof describes them.

explanation: Step 2 adds 7 to both sides: $3x - 7 + 7 = 20 + 7$, so $3x = 27$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Why proofs name the properties
steps: Solving an equation IS a proof — each move is legal because a property of equality says so.
Adding 7 to both sides is the Addition Property; dividing both sides by 3 is the Division Property. Naming them is what turns arithmetic into an argument.
